el-b01-n01: Good news first: English owns the two rarest sounds in Greek, and you have said both since you were four.
el-b01-n02: Your hand does this. Flat across the word, one flick down on the syllable that carries the printed accent.
el-b01-n03: Move one. Almost every Greek word of two syllables prints its beat. Flick where the mark is, not where English wants.
el-b01-p01: It is early, you are crossing the doorway of a bakery, and the woman behind the counter looks up. Speak now.
el-b01-n04: Move two. Theta is the th of thin. Delta is the th of this. Two of the rarest sounds on earth, already yours.
el-b01-p02: At the station window, one journey, one person, and the destination is the capital. Speak now.
el-b01-p03: The answer came back at full speed and none of it landed. Say so, and let the first sound be the th of this. Speak now.
el-b01-n05: Move three. Chi is the new one. Push air over the back of the tongue and keep it running — never kick it like a k.
el-b01-p04: You walk into a taverna at midday and two people at the till look up together. Greet the room. Speak now.
el-b01-p05: She has just wrapped the thing and handed it across. The air sound is in the middle, and the beat is at the very end. Speak now.
el-b01-n06: Move four. Rho is r, not p. Eta is i, not h. Your eye has to unlearn two shapes it thinks it already knows.
el-b01-p06: At the table, the jug is empty and the label on the bottle behind the bar starts with the letter that is not a v. Speak now.
el-b01-n07: Move five. Nu is n, psi is ps, xi is x, and epsilon plus upsilon comes out ef. Read the sound, not the shape.
el-b01-p07: Back at the bakery, your finger is on the round brown one on the top tray and there is one person ahead of you. Speak now.
el-b01-n08: Move six. Συγγνώμη is the hardest word in the kit. Its middle is the ng-n of wing nut, said in one go.
el-b01-p08: The aisle is narrow and your bag has just caught somebody's arm. One word, three pieces. Speak now.
el-b01-n09: One more thing about signs. The Latin spelling on a road sign is a spelling rule, not a guide to how the word sounds.
el-b01-p09: You are at the door on your way out and she is still behind the counter. Two syllables, and the beat is on the first. Speak now.
el-b01-s01: Καλημέρα. Ευχαριστώ πολύ. Νερό, παρακαλώ. Συγγνώμη. Γεια σας.
el-b01-n10: B01 done. Beat on the printed accent, theta and delta free, chi on air, rho as r, eta as i, Συγγνώμη in one go.
el-b01-q-i: A traveller orders at a bakery counter and then asks for the water on the way to the table.
el-b01-q04: Ορίστε. Γεια σας, καλή σας μέρα.
el-b02-n01: Ten words cover a whole shop visit. One of them has to come first, and it is the same word going in and coming out.
el-b02-p01: You are crossing the doorway of a small shop with the owner behind the counter. Speak now.
el-b02-n02: Research on politeness puts Greek and English on opposite defaults: closeness on one side, distance on the other.
el-b02-n03: So the greeting is not decoration here. It is the move that says you are entering, and it costs one word.
el-b02-p02: The sun has gone and the lights are on along the street. You are walking into a taverna. Speak now.
el-b02-n04: There is no rule fixing the hour the morning word turns into the evening one. Locals hesitate in that band too.
el-b02-p03: He has just put the change into your hand and closed the till. Speak now.
el-b02-p04: Someone at the counter steps back and opens a hand towards the window to let you go first. Say the one word. Speak now.
el-b02-p05: He tilts the carafe towards your glass for a second one, and you want it. Two words. Speak now.
el-b02-p06: You are browsing a rack of linen and someone comes over to help. Turn it down without closing the door. Speak now.
el-b02-n05: Greece sits high in the commercial English indices, and speaking is its lowest score. Those samples are self-selected.
el-b02-n06: Read that as a direction, never as a headcount. Two Greek words at the door are worth more than a plan built on English.
el-b02-p07: The aisle is narrow, two people are talking across it, and your stop is the door behind them. Speak now.
el-b02-p08: It is nearly one in the morning and you are leaving the table for bed. Speak now.
el-b02-p09: Bag in hand, one foot out of the shop, and the owner is still watching from the counter. Close the visit. Speak now.
el-b02-s01: Γεια σας. Ναι, παρακαλώ. Όχι, ευχαριστώ. Ευχαριστώ, γεια σας.
el-b02-n07: B02 done. Γεια σας in and out, καλημέρα and καλησπέρα, ευχαριστώ, παρακαλώ, ναι and όχι, συγγνώμη, καληνύχτα.
el-b02-q-i: A traveller walks into a small shop in the middle of the afternoon and leaves two minutes later.
el-b03-n01: You will lose a sentence on day one. That is not a thing to dodge — it is a moment with one opener that fixes it.
el-b03-n02: Here is the frame: Συγγνώμη, then the thing you need. Same opener for the baker, the clerk and the person in the doorway.
el-b03-n03: You drilled the word as a sound in part one. Sing, no, me, run together. Now it becomes the frame that opens everything.
el-b03-p01: At the bakery counter she has just said the price and it went straight past you. Speak now.
el-b03-r01: Α, συγγνώμη. Είπα δύο ευρώ και σαράντα.
el-b03-n04: The frame holds and only the ending changes: ask for it again, ask for it slower, ask for it written down.
el-b03-p02: Same bakery counter, and one more go at it would settle everything. Speak now.
el-b03-p03: At the ticket window the second try came back louder, at exactly the same speed. Ask for the other thing. Speak now.
el-b03-p04: Still at the ticket window, and it is a platform number you cannot afford to guess. Speak now.
el-b03-n05: Numbers and platforms are the ones to get on paper. Three repeats will not beat one line of handwriting.
el-b03-p05: You are on the crowded bus, packed to the doors, and your stop is next. Speak now.
el-b03-n06: Two more endings for the frame, both used on the street: whether the person has English, and what a thing is called.
el-b03-p06: On the pavement outside, what you need next is longer than your Greek. Open properly first. Speak now.
el-b03-p07: Back at the bakery counter, holding up the thing you want to be able to name. Speak now.
el-b03-p08: On the pavement outside, the directions came with three street names and one wave of the hand. Speak now.
el-b03-n07: Say the opener, then stop for half a beat. The pause is what turns your sentence into a request, not an interruption.
el-b03-p09: They slowed down, said it again and pointed you round the corner. Close it warmly. Speak now.
el-b03-s01: Συγγνώμη, δεν κατάλαβα. Συγγνώμη, πιο αργά, παρακαλώ. Συγγνώμη, μπορείτε να το γράψετε; Συγγνώμη, περνάω;
el-b03-n08: B03 done. Συγγνώμη plus the need covers the repeat, the slow version, the written version and the way through.
el-b03-q-i: A traveller misses a price at a counter, asks for it again, and then asks for it on paper.
el-b03-q02: Δώδεκα ευρώ. Η πύλη είναι στο τέσσερα.
el-b04-n01: Tonight's list is short and it expires. Five items, all cheaper to settle here than at a counter in Greece.
el-b04-n02: One: the health card. It buys the state system at resident conditions, and it leaves a known share with you.
el-b04-n03: Two: any ferry ticket. In Greece it carries a name by law, so book it under the passenger who travels.
el-b04-p01: You are ringing the hotel a week before the flight. Open with the job, in one line. Speak now.
el-b04-t01: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση.
el-b04-n04: A hotel name is not a destination. A driver and an offline map both want the street and the number.
el-b04-p02: The booking page shows a brand name and a neighbourhood. Get the thing a driver can actually drive to. Speak now.
el-b04-p03: You will not hold that in your head, and a tick inside an app is not proof. Ask for it another way. Speak now.
el-b04-n05: A late arrival is worth saying out loud. Small front desks are not always staffed through the night.
el-b04-p04: Your flight lands at eight and the metro takes an hour. Tell them when to expect you. Speak now.
el-b04-p05: Now check that somebody will be standing there when you push the door. Speak now.
el-b04-t05: Είναι ανοιχτή η ρεσεψιόν τη νύχτα;
el-b04-r03: Ναι, η ρεσεψιόν είναι ανοιχτή όλο το εικοσιτετράωρο.
el-b04-n06: Three: cash. Decide the amount now — a single bill of five hundred euros or more cannot be paid in notes.
el-b04-p06: Before you decide how many notes to bring, find out how this place wants to be paid. Speak now.
el-b04-p07: Get something you can dial from someone else's handset if yours arrives flat. Speak now.
el-b04-t07: Ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνο του ξενοδοχείου;
el-b04-n07: Four: the ferry office wants the passenger, not the buyer. Every ticket carries a name, and the name is checked.
el-b04-p08: You are booking the island crossing over the phone and the details were read out fast. Check whose crossing it is. Speak now.
el-b04-t08: Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου;
el-b04-n08: Five: save the address in Greek letters too. Latin spellings vary; the Greek one is what matches the sign.
el-b04-p09: The call did everything you rang for. Close it warmly and finish. Speak now.
el-b04-s01: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση. Ποια είναι η ακριβής διεύθυνση; Μπορείτε να μου το γράψετε;
el-b04-n09: B04 done. Card ordered, ticket in your own name, cash decided, address in hand — in both alphabets.
el-b04-q-i: Ten days before the flight, one call to the hotel closes the gaps that a phone call can still close.
el-b04-q02: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση. Ποια είναι η ακριβής διεύθυνση;
el-b04-q04: Μπορείτε να μου το γράψετε; Φτάνω στις δέκα το βράδυ.
el-b05-n01: The desk is three questions, not a Greek exam. Why you came, how many days, where you sleep.
el-b05-n02: A short question with no cushioning is the local shape of closeness here, not a sign of impatience.
el-b05-p01: You are here to walk around, eat well and go home again. Say it in four words. Speak now.
el-b05-n03: Use your own number, not the one in this part. The shape of the answer stays exactly this short.
el-b05-p02: Give the length of the stay and nothing else. Two words. Speak now.
el-b05-n04: Not the story of how you found the place. Town, kind of place, full stop.
el-b05-p03: Say where you sleep, briefly — the town and the kind of place. Speak now.
el-b05-p04: Hand over the offline copy you saved last night, and let the document do the talking. Speak now.
el-b05-n05: Ορίστε is the whole sentence. Three syllables and an open hand outrun any paragraph you could build.
el-b05-n06: If it went past you, say so once. Συγγνώμη opens the repair and no desk minds hearing it.
el-b05-p05: It went past you too fast. Say so cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
el-b05-p06: The question came back at the same speed as the first time. Ask for the one thing that would fix it. Speak now.
el-b05-n07: Μόνος μου if you are a man, μόνη μου if you are a woman. One letter, and it is the only thing that moves.
el-b05-p07: Nobody is with you on this trip. Say it in three words, in the form that matches you. Speak now.
el-b05-p08: They ask whether Athens is the whole trip. Answer truthfully and briefly. Speak now.
el-b05-n08: Some officers switch to English and some do not. The three Greek answers work either way.
el-b05-p09: Four words, take the passport, walk. Speak now.
el-b05-s01: Ήρθα για διακοπές. Δέκα μέρες. Στην Αθήνα, σε ξενοδοχείο. Ναι, ορίστε.
el-b05-n09: B05 done. Purpose, days, where you sleep, ορίστε. Short is not evasive — short means the answer matched.
el-b05-q-i: A traveller reaches passport control in Athens with three short answers and one repair phrase.
el-b05-q02: Γεια σας. Είμαι για διακοπές. Δέκα μέρες.
el-b05-q03: Πού θα μείνετε; Έχετε την κράτηση;
el-b05-q04: Στην Αθήνα, σε ξενοδοχείο. Ναι, ορίστε.
el-b06-n01: Your first hour is four counters and four small questions. In Greece they all open the same way.
el-b06-n02: Here is the frame: έχετε, and then the thing. Do you have — and then whatever you happen to need.
el-b06-p01: At the information desk, paper survives a flat battery and yours is nearly flat. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-n03: Notice what the frame asks: not whether the thing exists somewhere, but whether this person has it.
el-b06-p02: At the phone shop by baggage reclaim, you want a local number for the week. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-n04: Καλημέρα comes first, every single time. Arriving with the request and no greeting is entering without knocking.
el-b06-p03: Back at the phone shop: your battery is at four percent and everything you own is in the hold bag. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-n05: The thing after the frame arrives as one block. Learn έχετε χάρτη whole and never take it apart.
el-b06-p04: At the information desk again: the room is not ready until three and you are carrying everything. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-p05: The kiosk by the exit sells travel, and the machines have a long queue in front of them. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-n06: The frame does not care what the thing is. A map, a charger, tickets, water, coins, a toilet.
el-b06-p06: Still at the kiosk: the luggage trolley takes coins only and the machine gave you a twenty. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-r02: Όχι εδώ, αλλά έχει στο περίπτερο απέναντι.
el-b06-n07: Card is owed to you at a long list of trades here, and the notice has to be visible at the door and the till.
el-b06-p07: You are about to hand over your last note at the kiosk and you would rather keep it. Check first. Speak now.
el-b06-n08: A no usually carries the address of the yes. Stay one beat past the first word.
el-b06-p08: At the airport café, before an hour on the metro in August. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-p09: Still at the airport café, before the train and the long ride into town. Ask. Speak now.
el-b06-n09: Cash machines have a fee ceiling now, and where a small community has just one, the fee is zero.
el-b06-p10: They sorted you out in ten seconds. Close it the way people close things here. Speak now.
el-b06-s01: Έχετε χάρτη; Έχετε φορτιστή; Έχετε ψιλά;
el-b06-n10: B06 done. One frame, four counters, and the whole first hour answered with έχετε and a noun.
el-b06-q-i: A traveller crosses the arrivals hall with one opening and nine different needs.
el-b06-q04: Όχι εδώ, αλλά έχει στο περίπτερο απέναντι.
el-b07-n01: Between the plane and the bed there are four counters, and every one of them answers the same opening.
el-b07-n02: Here is the frame: Μπορώ να, then what you want to do. Can I — and then the verb.
el-b07-p01: At the taxi rank, before the door closes: you have no cash on you at all. Check first. Speak now.
el-b07-r01: Ναι, βέβαια. Με κάρτα ή με μετρητά;
el-b07-n03: The frame does not ask the world for permission. It asks this person, at this counter, right now.
el-b07-p02: At the metro ticket office, both machines have a paper sign on them and a person sits behind the glass. Speak now.
el-b07-n04: Card is not a favour here. Whole categories of trade are obliged to take it, and to say so at the door.
el-b07-p03: The driver has taken your money and is already reaching for the door handle. Ask for the printed slip. Speak now.
el-b07-n05: The airport metro is nine euros one way, sixteen return. The Express bus into town is five fifty.
el-b07-r02: Το εισιτήριο για το κέντρο, πέντε και πενήντα.
el-b07-p04: The Express bus is full and the one free place has someone's bag on it. Ask the woman beside it. Speak now.
el-b07-p05: You are three bodies away from the doors of the Express bus and they are about to open. Speak now.
el-b07-p06: The Express bus is stopped at a light and the square you were aiming for is right outside the window. Speak now.
el-b07-n06: Same two words every time. Μπορώ να, then pay, buy, sit, get past, get off, leave the bag.
el-b07-p07: At the hotel front desk, the room is not ready until two and you want your hands free until then. Speak now.
el-b07-t07: Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ;
el-b07-r03: Βεβαίως, αφήστε την εκεί, στη γωνία.
el-b07-n07: The taxi rank at the airport works on a posted flat fare into town. Ask before the door shuts, not after.
el-b07-p08: You are in the taxi with the door closed and the driver is waiting for one piece of information. Speak now.
el-b07-p09: The ride is over and your bag is already out on the pavement. Close it the way people close things here. Speak now.
el-b07-s01: Μπορώ να πληρώσω με κάρτα; Μπορώ να καθίσω εδώ; Μπορώ να αφήσω τη βαλίτσα εδώ;
el-b07-n08: B07 done. One frame carried you from the terminal to the front desk with no new sentence anywhere.
el-b07-q-i: You have landed, the bag is out, and there is a taxi rank outside door three. Listen to the whole exchange before you answer.
el-b07-q01: Καλησπέρα. Μπορώ να πληρώσω με κάρτα;
el-b07-q02: Βεβαίως. Σαράντα ευρώ μέχρι το κέντρο, με τα διόδια.
el-b07-q03: Εντάξει. Στο κέντρο, παρακαλώ. Μπορώ να πάρω απόδειξη;
el-b07-q04: Ναι, στο τέλος. Αφήστε τη βαλίτσα, την βάζω εγώ.
el-b08-n01: Ask where something is and you can get a paragraph back. The trick is asking so the answer fits in your head.
el-b08-n02: Here is the frame: Πού είναι, then the place. The place goes in exactly as the map spells it.
el-b08-p01: The app says the bus leaves in four minutes and there is no shelter in sight. Ask the man at the kiosk. Speak now.
el-b08-r01: Ευθεία και μετά δεξιά, δίπλα στο περίπτερο.
el-b08-n03: Nothing changes shape after Πού είναι. You read the word on the map, and you say the word.
el-b08-p02: You are in a station hall with four stairways and none of them is signed in a way you can read. Speak now.
el-b08-n04: Road signs are romanised by a standard used very widely in Greece — and it is a poor guide to the sound.
el-b08-n05: So say the Greek, not the sign. ΒΟΛΟΣ is Volos, not Bolos: that Β is a V, and the Η is an ee.
el-b08-p03: You are inside a café, you have already ordered, and there is one door at the back with no picture on it. Speak now.
el-b08-p04: Your blister has gone from annoying to limping, and you want the green cross on this street. Speak now.
el-b08-p05: You got off the train at Piraeus, everyone is walking in three directions, and your boat leaves at eight. Speak now.
el-b08-r02: Πέντε λεπτά με τα πόδια. Ακολουθήστε τον κόσμο.
el-b08-n06: Now shrink the answer. Far or not, left or right, this way — three words and a pointed finger.
el-b08-p06: They have just pointed down a long street and you need to know whether to walk it or find a bus. Speak now.
el-b08-p07: The answer had four street names in it and you caught none of them. Offer them two options instead. Speak now.
el-b08-n07: Research describes Greek politeness as leaning on closeness where English leans on distance. Short reads as normal.
el-b08-p08: You are stopping a stranger mid-stride on the pavement, and the machine you need takes cards. Speak now.
el-b08-p09: At the hotel desk, your phone is at six percent and paper survives a flat battery. Speak now.
el-b08-r03: Ναι, ορίστε. Είμαστε εδώ, και το λιμάνι είναι εκεί.
el-b08-s01: Πού είναι η στάση; Πού είναι το φαρμακείο; Πού είναι το λιμάνι;
el-b08-n08: B08 done. One frame, five places, and a follow-up short enough to be answered with a hand.
el-b08-q-i: A corner in the centre, a stranger stopped mid-stride, and an answer with more streets in it than you can hold. Listen right to the end.
el-b08-q02: Ευθεία, μετά την εκκλησία δεξιά, και είναι απέναντι από το περίπτερο.
el-b08-q04: Όχι, πέντε λεπτά με τα πόδια. Ελάτε, σας δείχνω.
el-b09-n01: A ticket here is two moves, not one. You buy it, and then you start it. The clock has not begun yet.
el-b09-p01: In the station hall, every machine has a queue and you would rather deal with a person. Speak now.
el-b09-p02: You are at the window, you are travelling alone, and the person behind the glass is waiting. Speak now.
el-b09-n02: In Athens the ninety-minute ticket is one euro twenty, and the ninety minutes run from the first validation.
el-b09-p03: The paper is in your hand and there is a small orange box somewhere on this platform. Ask the guard. Speak now.
el-b09-r02: Εκεί, στην είσοδο. Ακυρώστε το πριν μπείτε.
el-b09-n03: So validate on the way in. Until you do, it is a piece of paper and the ninety minutes have not started.
el-b09-p04: You bought a paper ticket on a route where you have only ever seen people tap a card. Check with the driver. Speak now.
el-b09-p05: You have one more stop to make before the museum and you want to know if this paper covers both. Speak now.
el-b09-n04: An unvalidated ticket in front of an inspector costs around a hundred euros. That figure is under revision.
el-b09-n05: A ferry ticket is a different animal. By law it carries your name, sex, nationality and date of birth.
el-b09-p06: At the ferry desk in Piraeus, there are two of you and the boat you want goes to Naxos. Speak now.
el-b09-t06: Δύο εισιτήρια για τη Νάξο, παρακαλώ.
el-b09-r03: Τα ονόματά σας, παρακαλώ. Και την ημερομηνία γέννησης.
el-b09-p07: The clerk has asked for something and your document is at the bottom of the bag. Check what they need. Speak now.
el-b09-p08: At the gangway, the crew member looks at the paper and then at you. Confirm the obvious out loud. Speak now.
el-b09-t08: Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου.
el-b09-n06: So nobody buys a ferry ticket for you, and nobody hands a spare one along. The name has to be yours.
el-b09-p09: The boarding paper has a gate number on it and the quay in front of you has eight of them. Speak now.
el-b09-n07: Numbers come fast at a window. You do not have to say them back — you have to catch two of them.
el-b09-p10: The clerk gave you the amount and the gate in one breath and you caught neither. Ask for it again, gently. Speak now.
el-b09-r04: Εννιά ευρώ. Αποβάθρα τέσσερα, στις οκτώ.
el-b09-s01: Ένα εισιτήριο, παρακαλώ. Πού είναι το ακυρωτικό; Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου.
el-b09-n08: B09 done. Buy it, put your name on it where the law asks, and start the clock before anyone else does.
el-b09-q-i: One window in Piraeus, one platform, and a paper that is not yet a ticket. Listen for the two numbers that matter.
el-b09-q01: Δύο εισιτήρια για τη Νάξο, παρακαλώ.
el-b09-q02: Τα ονόματά σας και την ημερομηνία γέννησης, παρακαλώ. Αποβάθρα τέσσερα, στις οκτώ.
el-b09-q03: Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ. Πού είναι το ακυρωτικό;
el-b09-q04: Εκεί, στην είσοδο. Ακυρώστε το πριν μπείτε.
el-b10-n01: Greek signs come in two scripts. Only one of them is the place. The other is a spelling, not a sound.
el-b10-n02: The frame is ψάχνω, then the thing. It says what you are after long before you can read the word for it.
el-b10-p01: The hall has four doors and the only word above them is in letters you are still matching. Say what you are after. Speak now.
el-b10-r01: Εκεί, δεξιά. Γράφει ΕΞΟΔΟΣ πάνω από την πόρτα.
el-b10-n03: Five letters lie to your eye. Ρ is R, Η is I, Χ is CH, Β is V, and Υ comes out as ee.
el-b10-p02: At the ferry gate the board reads ΡΟΔΟΣ and your printed ticket reads RODOS. Tell the agent which sailing you want. Speak now.

el-a06-p08: Three shutters down in a row on the same pavement, and you still need the counter behind one of them. Ask a passer-by. Speak now.
el-a06-p09: A stranger just saved you a pointless walk across town on a holiday. Close it warmly. Speak now.

el-a06-n10: A06 done. Thirteen days of drift, nine named dates, July against January, and one question at the door.
el-a06-q-i: A traveller stops reading the calendar on their phone and starts asking the door in front of them.
el-a06-q01: Φέτος το Πάσχα μας είναι δύο εβδομάδες μετά το δικό σας.
el-a06-q02: Αύριο είναι αργία, αλλά εμείς είμαστε ανοιχτά.

el-a07-n01: Half of what you need to read in a Greek room arrives before the sentence does, and most of it is not body language.
el-a07-n02: Politeness research puts Greek on the involvement side and English on the distance side. That is measured, not folklore.
el-a07-n03: So warmth can read to you as intrusion, and your good manners can read to them as coldness. Both readings are wrong.
el-a07-n04: First signal: εσείς and εσύ. Formal and familiar, and the same distinction you already met in γεια σας and γεια σου.
el-a07-r01: Πώς σας λένε; Από πού είστε;
el-a07-p01: Someone behind a counter has been kind to you three days running and you still do not know how to address them. Ask, politely. Speak now.
el-a07-n05: The move to εσύ is offered, not taken. You start on εσείς and wait for someone to open the other door.
el-a07-r02: Έλα, πάμε στον ενικό. Τι λες;
el-a07-p02: The door just opened and the only wrong answer is hesitating. Take it, warmly. Speak now.
el-a07-n06: Second signal: the no. A short upward tilt of the head with a small click of the tongue. It is not disapproval.
el-a07-n07: An English ear hears that click as impatience. It is closer to a shrug, and it saves everyone a sentence.
el-a07-p03: Something arrived fast and flat and you caught none of it. Open the repair before the moment closes. Speak now.
el-a07-t03: Συγγνώμη, δεν κατάλαβα. Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ.
el-a07-n08: Third: volume. A raised voice at the next table is far more often engagement than temperature. Listen to the faces.
el-a07-r04: Πέρνα μέσα, κάτσε! Τι θα πιεις;
el-a07-p04: There is one free chair at a busy table and nobody has looked up yet. Ask before you take it. Speak now.
el-a07-n09: Fourth: the open palm pushed towards someone's face is read as an insult. Wave with your fingers together.
el-a07-p05: Two people were mid-conversation when you walked up, and you would rather check than assume. One word does it. Speak now.
el-a07-n10: And the last set: leaving. Καλή συνέχεια and στο καλό are release, not dismissal. They mean go well.
el-a07-p06: An hour at a table you were not expecting to join, and you want to name what you are grateful for. Speak now.
el-a07-n11: Να πηγαίνω is how you open the leaving, not how you finish it. Say it early and expect to be kept.
el-a07-p07: You genuinely have to be somewhere, and you want to start the long goodbye rather than cut it. Speak now.
el-a07-p08: You are on your feet, coat in hand, and one warm line is still owed to the person who pulled the chair out. Speak now.
el-a07-s01: Ενοχλώ; Μπορώ να καθίσω εδώ; Να πηγαίνω. Καλή συνέχεια!
el-a07-n12: A07 done. Wait to be moved to εσύ, read the click as no, hear volume as engagement, and start leaving early.
el-a07-q-i: A traveller learns to wait to be moved, and to start leaving long before leaving.

el-a08-n01: Last morning. The people who made your week are three doors apart, and each of them takes about a minute.
el-a08-n02: The shape is the same every time: name the person, name the thing they did, name when you are coming back.
el-a08-p01: The woman at the guesthouse desk fixed four separate things this week without being asked. Open the goodbye. Speak now.
el-a08-n03: Then be specific. Thanks for everything is polite; naming the dish is what the cook actually hears.
el-a08-p02: You are settling up at the taverna you came back to three nights running. Say the one thing worth saying. Speak now.
el-a08-n04: Say a season, not someday. Summer's share of arrivals fell from fifty-six percent to fifty; spring and winter are growing.
el-a08-p03: They asked when, and vagueness would waste the moment. Put a season on it. Speak now.
el-a08-n05: Then ask for the card. It gives you a name to book with, and it says out loud that you intend to be back.
el-a08-p04: You want a way to reach this place directly next year instead of through a booking site. Ask at the desk. Speak now.
el-a08-r03: Πάρε την κάρτα μου. Τηλεφώνησε πριν έρθεις.
el-a08-p05: One of them looked straight at the harbour, and you would rather not be reassigned when you come back. Say so at the desk. Speak now.
el-a08-t05: Θα ήθελα το ίδιο δωμάτιο του χρόνου.
el-a08-n06: One more line is worth more than any review you could write, and it costs you nothing at all to say.
el-a08-p06: You mean it, and the family running this place will hear it as the best thing said to them all week. Speak now.
el-a08-r04: Την άλλη φορά θα φας σπίτι μου.
el-a08-p07: The person in front of you spent an hour of their own time on you on Tuesday. Close a first meeting properly. Speak now.
el-a08-n07: Να είστε καλά is the warmest thing in the whole kit and costs nothing. It means be well, and it lands every time.
el-a08-p08: The bag is on your shoulder and one line is still owed to the people at the door. Speak now.
el-a08-n08: And the goodbye of someone who plans to return: καλή αντάμωση. Until we meet again, said as a plan.
el-a08-p09: Last line of the trip, at the door, to someone you fully intend to see again. Speak now.
el-a08-n09: Eight openings carried this entire trip, and they fit on one card in your pocket. Here they are, in order.
el-a08-n10: Έχετε, μπορώ να, πού είναι, θα ήθελα. Then χωρίς, πόσο κάνει, ψάχνω, and συγγνώμη in front of any of them.
el-a08-s01: Ευχαριστώ για όλα. Θα ξανάρθω το φθινόπωρο. Να είστε καλά! Καλή αντάμωση!
el-a08-n11: A08 done, and the course with it. Name them, name the thing, name the season. Eight openings in your pocket.
el-a08-q-i: A traveller spends fifteen minutes on the last morning instead of five, and leaves as someone expected back.
el-a08-q03: Πάρε την κάρτα μου. Τηλεφώνησε πριν έρθεις.
